To find the total return and annualized return, we use the starting closing price at the end of January 2024 (P_{\text{start}} = 61.53) and the ending closing price at the end of January 2025 (P_{\text{end}} = 120.07).
(a) Total Return Method
The total return measures the overall percentage change from the initial price to the final price:
$$\text{Total Return} = \frac{P_{\text{end}} - P_{\text{start}}}{P_{\text{start}}}$$
Substituting the given prices:
$$\text{Total Return} = \frac{120.07 - 61.53}{61.53} = \frac{58.54}{61.53} \approx 0.951406 \text{ (or } 95.14\% \text{)}$$
(b) Annualized Return Method
The annualized return (Compound Annual Growth Rate, or CAGR) is calculated using the number of years (n) elapsed between the first and last price observation:
$$\text{Annualized Return} = \left( \frac{P_{\text{end}}}{P_{\text{start}}} \right)^{\frac{1}{n}} - 1 = (1 + \text{Total Return})^{\frac{12}{m}} - 1$$
where m is the number of monthly compounding periods elapsed:

* Exact Elapsed Time (m = 12 months, or n = 1 year): Because each price is recorded at the end of the month, moving from the end of January 2024 to the end of January 2025 spans exactly 12 monthly return intervals (1.0\text{ year}).
$$\text{Annualized Return} = \left( \frac{120.07}{61.53} \right)^{\frac{12}{12}} - 1 = (1.951406)^1 - 1 \approx 0.951406 \text{ (or } 95.14\% \text{)}$$
* (Note: If counting the 13 listed rows as 13 full months where n = \frac{13}{12}, the formula yields (1.951406)^{\frac{12}{13}} - 1 \approx 85.36\%.)

Total return: 95.14% Annualized return: 95.14%
notes: Matched my ground truth (95.14%). Caught the trap: explained that the prices span 12 monthly intervals, and flagged that counting the 13 rows as 13 months would give 85.36%. Used the CAGR formula with an explicit 12/m exponent. Format: put both final answers on one line instead of separate lines as the prompt asked.
